rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality expanded blastocyst, but the image is somewhat indistinct and the response overstates certainty about a tightly defined ICM, uniformly cohesive TE, symmetry, and absence of degeneration that are not all clearly verifiable from this single image.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, endometriosis, endometrial thickness, semen parameters, lifestyle, and first-cycle status with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with probability estimates tied to embryo quality and patient factors; minor issues include somewhat speculative quantitative adjustments and a few recommendations extending beyond the presented evidence.

Core recommendations such as single embryo transfer and general prognosis are guideline-concordant, but suggestions like ERA after one failed transfer, routine augmented luteal support/estradiol, low-dose aspirin, and broad PGT-A framing are more controversial or not routinely guideline-supported.
Provides clear practical next steps for transfer, luteal support, monitoring, lifestyle optimization, and contingency planning, though some actions are more speculative than standard-of-care.
